ticket.summary: Intermittent strong sulfur odor in air around gas water heater in basement (no symptoms reported); customer directed to gas utility emergency line, on-call plumber paged; secondary slow basement floor drain + musty smell to be snaked once house is cleared.
mitigation_advice: Evacuate basement/house and keep pets out
Do not operate light switches, plugs, or garage door opener
Call 911 or gas utility 24/7 emergency line from outside (free response)
Do not relight pilot or attempt gas shutoff unless utility directs
After clearance, pour ~1 gallon of water down the basement floor drain to refill a possibly dry trap
Text back immediately if utility finds a leak or red-tags an appliance for same-night dispatch

quote_lines.description: After-hours gas leak diagnostic and leak test at water heater / gas line (repairs quoted after diagnosis)
Basement floor drain cable clearing, up to 75 ft (to be scheduled this week, separate visit)

ticket.customer_message: Take this seriously: intermittent, sometimes-strong rotten egg smell in the air near a gas water heater is the classic sign of a gas leak. Get everyone and pets out of the basement (ideally the house), don't flip switches/unplug anything/use the garage door, and from outside call 911 or your gas utility's free 24/7 emergency line. Don't relight the pilot or touch the gas valve unless they tell you to. Note: sewer gas from a dried-out floor drain trap smells similar and fits your slow drain too, but let the utility rule out the dangerous one first. I'm paging our on-call plumber now to follow up after they clear the house, or tonight if they find a leak. For the drain: $285 flat to snake it (60-90 min) and I'll book you later this week; if it's just a dry trap, a gallon of water down the drain may fix the smell.
